title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Picture 10's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$0030, channel 0's script at +$000E and 0 for channels 1, 2 and 3, which it does not use.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 11 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 5, frame 2 then 1, frame 3 then 1, frame 3 then 1, frame 2 then 6, frame 4 then 3, frame 5 then 3, frame 6 then 1, frame 6 then 5, frame 7 then 9, frame 8 then 8. One pass takes 43 steps.

Picture 10's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $06 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 29 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 1: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 21 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 2 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 3 and 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 15 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 4 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 10 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 28 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 7: a run count of 0 to start, then 14 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 42 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 8 and 9: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 10: a run count of 0 to start, then 10 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 54 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 3 to 9. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 10, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entry 11: a run count of 0 to start, then 10 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 61 bitmap bytes in all (1 run of a repeated byte among them), in columns 3 to 9. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 10's own packed bytes decode to, the 1,172nd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
